A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Elastic3D and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, references, and appendices. Existing content can be matched across the appendix reflow and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original stereo-video experiments, component ablations, latency measurements, and a headset user study, including Tables 1–15.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds analyses of metric agreement with human preferences and quantitative disparity-control accuracy.

M1.justification: The one-step synthesis network, scalar disparity conditioning, epipolar-guided decoder, losses, and separate training stages remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices A–C. Added preprocessing descriptions do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions cover Stereo4D, Ego4D, AVP/iPhone spatial videos, and in-the-wild disparity-controlled generation. The new ten-video sweep quantifies an existing scenario without establishing a new domain or task.

E2.justification: Video-generation baseline membership remains unchanged. However, v2 Section D.2/Figure 6 adds PSNR and LPIPS as comparators to Matchability Error for human-preference agreement. v1's metric-sensitivity comparisons used PSNR versus P-PSNR and SSIM versus Matchability Error; LPIPS was not a comparator in those analyses.

E3.justification: v2 adds a preference-correlation protocol using a tie-adjusted subjective score and a disparity-control sweep comprising ten videos, ten conditioning values, FoundationStereo measurements, and analysis across 45 frame indices. Existing benchmark settings remain unchanged; the newly specified baseline-alignment details do not establish reruns or a revised earlier protocol.

E4.justification: Sections D.2 and E.4 add targeted tests of whether the proposed metric reflects human preferences and whether requested disparity produces accurate, consistent responses. Existing component ablations, shift/blur sensitivity tests, headset study, and qualitative failure analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 introduces correlation estimation for preference agreement and disparity response, with fitted trends and shaded bands in Figures 6 and 12. The bands' statistical meaning is unspecified. The 100 inferences describe distinct video/conditioning combinations; no new repeated-seed protocol or significance testing is documented.

E6.justification: Existing table values and qualitative examples are unchanged. New findings include preference correlations of -0.53 for Matchability Error, -0.33 for LPIPS, and -0.08 for PSNR; first-frame disparity MAE of 0.54 pixels; and average disparity-response correlation of 0.986. Appendix A.1 also newly reports residual vertical parallax below two pixels.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 13 introduces the tie-adjusted preference-score definition SPS = (N_Ours + 0.5 × N_Tie) / N_Total for the new analysis. The epipolar-attention mathematics, one-step diffusion derivation, and Matchability Error definition remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: direct warping-free synthesis, scalar stereo control, guided decoding, and comprehensive evaluation. The added appendix evidence supports these existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new correlations as evidence that Matchability Error better reflects perceived stereo fidelity, hypothesizing that PSNR can reward blur. It also explains why later-frame control is assessed relatively as scene depth distributions evolve. The substantive limitations in Appendix H remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents LoFTR/RANSAC rectification and baseline alignment using an L1 scale-and-shift fit, positive disparities, and no maximum-disparity clipping. These clarify previously described processing rather than demonstrate implementation changes. The appendix video-viewing instruction changes from an attached index.html to the project page.

R1.justification: The same 72 referenced works and substantive research positioning are retained. Changed citation back-references reflect pagination and additional uses of existing references.

P1.justification: v2 adds short appendix subsections, corrects wording and typographical errors, and removes some Elastic3D name mentions and its acronym expansion. The appendix overview now repeats the Section E description and omits its former pointers to F–H, although those sections remain.

P2.justification: v2 adds the preference-correlation plots in Figure 6 and disparity-response plot in Figure 12. Existing figure images and table structures are retained, with appendix figures and tables relocated and renumbered during reflow; the overall visual design remains stable.

improvement.justification: The new preference-correlation and disparity-control analyses provide useful direct validation of two existing contributions, while the preprocessing disclosures improve reproducibility. These targeted gains outweigh the duplicated appendix overview and insufficient explanation of the plotted bands. The core method, benchmark findings, and acknowledged limitations remain unchanged.
